sources.entry: paramiko - The leading native Python SSHv2 protocol library.

summary.one_liner: Paramiko is a pure-Python implementation of the SSHv2 protocol, providing both client and server functionality.
summary.what_it_does: Implements the SSHv2 protocol in pure Python, offering both client and server functionality. The README positions it as the foundation for the higher-level Fabric library, which it recommends for common tasks like running remote shell commands or transferring files. Direct use of Paramiko is aimed at users who need low-level primitives or want to run an SSH daemon (sshd) written in Python. It relies on the cryptography package for crypto functionality, which uses C and Rust extensions with many precompiled options. Installation, changelogs, FAQs and API docs are hosted on the project website and versioned docs, not in the README itself.
use_cases: Programmatic SSH connections from Python scripts
Building custom SSH clients or servers in Python
Low-level SSH protocol access for advanced use
Foundation for higher-level tools like Fabric
notable: Pure-Python implementation of SSHv2 with both client and server sides
Underlies the Fabric high-level SSH library
Uses OpenSSH as the primary reference implementation
Listed as the leading native Python SSHv2 library in awesome-python
caveats: README recommends Fabric rather than direct use for common client tasks; Paramiko is aimed at low-level or advanced users
Installation details are on the external project website, not in the README
